One verified release candidate now survives every gate

The release command no longer rebuilds between validation and upload. The artifact that passes verification is the only artifact publication can receive. This PR changes candidate identity and handoff; build rules, verification rules, and production rollout stay outside its scope.

Why the old release path was unsafe

Verification approved one build, but publication asked the build system to create another. Even when both builds began from the same configuration, the uploaded bytes were not the bytes that had passed the gate.

The practical failure: a dependency or generated file could change between the two builds, allowing an unverified artifact to reach production.

Before and now

MomentBeforeNow
BuildCreated a temporary artifact for verification.Creates one candidate with a stable identity.
VerificationReturned success without carrying the artifact forward.Returns a receipt bound to that candidate.
PublicationRebuilt from configuration and uploaded the new output.Accepts only the verified receipt and uploads its candidate.
RetryCould rebuild again after a network failure.Reuses the same receipt and candidate.

Follow one release through the new boundary

  1. 1
    Build

    The runner creates candidate web-1842 with one content digest.

  2. 2
    Verify

    The verifier binds its receipt to that candidate and digest.

  3. 3
    Publish

    The publisher receives the receipt, not build configuration.

  4. 4
    Retry

    A failed upload reuses the receipt, so the bytes cannot change.

Where the responsibilities live

PartPlain-language responsibilityExact changeWhy it matters
release/types.tsDefines the candidate and proof carried between stages.Adds stable identity and a receipt bound to one digest.The contract makes substituting another build invalid.
release/run.tsCoordinates the release.Builds once and passes the same candidate through verification and publication.The safe path is the ordinary path.
release/publish.tsControls what can be uploaded.Accepts a verified receipt instead of build configuration.The publisher can no longer rebuild.

The boundary of this PR

IncludedDeliberately unchanged or deferred
One candidate identity across build, verification, upload, and retryHow candidates are built
A publisher contract that requires proofThe verification rules themselves
Retry behavior that preserves the original receiptProduction rollout and a live registry upload

What is proven, and what is not

Scenario exercisedWhat the evidence establishesRemaining limit
A candidate passes through every in-process stageThe identity and digest remain unchanged.Does not exercise an external registry.
An upload fails once and retriesThe retry reuses the original receipt and candidate.Does not simulate a process restart.
The publisher is called without a receiptThe contract rejects the call before upload.A live production upload is still unverified.

Residual risk and containment: a process restart could expose a receipt-persistence gap and a live registry could behave differently from the fixture. Keep rollout non-production until a restart retry and one external upload preserve candidate web-1842.
